Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you will need to register by pressing star then one on your telephone keypad. We ask that you limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. There will be an opportunity for everyone to ask questions. Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to John Smith, Director of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp's Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Mike Johnson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Tom Rivera, Chief Operating Officer; David Lee, VP of Exploration; Emily Carter, VP of Marketing; and Sarah Jenkins, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Mike Johnson.

Mike Johnson: Thank you, John, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp delivered solid results in Q3, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production volumes averaging 450,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day and impressive proved reserves additions with a reserve replacement ratio exceeding 180%. I'm particularly pleased with our progress on ESG initiatives, including significant advancements in emissions reduction targets. We are focused on future development plans highlighting substantial resource potential across our key basins. Further, we are working on exploration and drilling activity updates that have produced key well results surpassing type curves. We continue to adjust to refining segment performance with high throughput and margins. Finally, we are taking steps to optimize realized prices through our robust hedging programs.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins for an update on our ESG initiatives.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Mike, and good morning, everyone. As we continue to execute on our strategy to deliver long-term value in a transitioning energy landscape, our ESG commitments remain front and center. Today, I'll dive deep into our emissions reduction progress, which is a cornerstone of our Environmental pillar. We're not just talking aspirations—we're delivering measurable results that align with our net-zero by 2050 ambition, fully Paris Agreement-aligned, and supported by SBTi-validated science-based targets.

Let me start with the big picture. Our baseline for Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions is 2019, when we emitted 45 million metric tons of CO2e across our global portfolio. Our 2030 target is a 35% absolute reduction from that baseline, ramping to 65% by 2040. Intensity-wise, we're targeting under 20 kg CO2e per boe by 2030, down from 28 kg in 2019. I'm pleased to report that through Q3 2024, we've achieved an 18% absolute reduction in Scope 1 and 2 emissions year-to-date—putting us ahead of our internal trajectory for a 20% cut by year-end. On an intensity basis, we're now at 22.5 kg CO2e/boe, a 20% improvement, even as production grew 4% YoY to 450,000 boe/d.

Breaking this down by scope and region for transparency:

Scope 1 (Operational Emissions): These account for 92% of our footprint, primarily from venting, flaring, and fugitive methane. We've reduced Scope 1 by 21% YTD, driven by a 55% drop in routine flaring volumes to just 0.4% of gross gas production—well below the World Bank's Zero Routine Flaring by 2030 pledge, which we're on track to beat. In the Permian Basin, our largest asset producing 1.2 million boe/d, flaring intensity fell to 0.2% from 1.1% in 2021, thanks to our $450 million investment in midstream infrastructure, including vapor recovery units and electrification of 250 drilling rigs. This not only slashed emissions but saved us $35 million in lost gas revenue.

Methane is the big win here: Down 28% YTD to 65 kt CH4, or 1.7 million tCO2e equivalent. We deployed continuous monitoring across 85% of our assets using drone-based LiDAR tech from Bridger Photonics and satellite OGI from GHGSat, identifying and repairing over 12,000 leaks—equivalent to taking 250,000 cars off the road. In the North Sea, where Norwegian carbon taxes hit $100/tCO2e this year, our Troll and Oseberg fields achieved a 32% methane cut via subsea compression and optical gas imaging on FPSOs.

Scope 2 (Purchased Energy): A 12% reduction to 2.8 million tCO2e, primarily from switching 40% of our offshore power to renewables. In the Middle East, our ADNOC-partnered concessions in Abu Dhabi now run on 100% grid solar via the Emirates' Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum hub, dropping Scope 2 intensity by 45%.

Regionally, the U.S. onshore (Permian and Bakken) saw the steepest progress at 24% reduction, buoyed by EPA's methane rules and our $200 million electrification program partnering with Caterpillar for hydrogen-ready turbines. Upstream Europe lagged slightly at 15% due to legacy North Sea infrastructure, but we're accelerating with a $1.2 billion JV with Equinor for blue hydrogen blending. Internationally, Brazil's pre-salt fields hit 19% via subsea boosting tech from OneSubsea, minimizing venting.

Key technical initiatives fueling this progress:

1. CCUS Scale-Up: We're capturing 4.2 million tCO2e annually across three hubs. The Permian Hub, in partnership with Occidental and ExxonMobil, is storing 2 million tpa at $30/t—half our target cost—using our proprietary solvent-based capture on gas plants, hitting 95% efficiency. In the North Sea, Northern Lights Phase 2 ramps to 5 mtpa by 2027.

2. Digital Twins and AI: Rolled out AspenTech's emissions module across 1,500 wells, optimizing blowdown events and reducing fugitive emissions by 15% through predictive analytics.

3. Low-Carbon Fuels: 20% of our rig fleet now runs on RNG from our landfill JV with Archaea Energy, cutting diesel Scope 1 by 18%.

Strategically, these aren't just green checkboxes—they're value creators. Our emissions trajectory de-risks us from emerging carbon border taxes like the EU CBAM, which could add $500 million to import costs for non-compliant peers by 2026. ESG funds like BlackRock's energy sleeve now hold 12% of our float, up from 7% last year, and our LTIF safety rate of 0.12—best-in-supermajor peer group—pairs with this for top-quartile MSCI ESG ratings. Cost savings hit $280 million in 2024 from efficiency gains, funding our $15 billion capex while maintaining a 12% ROCE.

Looking ahead, we'll announce our Scope 3 baseline next quarter, targeting 20% cut by 2035 via supplier engagements and biofuels. With oil demand resilient at 103 mb/d per IEA STEPS, we're proving fossil fuels can decarbonize affordably—positioning us as the transition play for investors.

Thank you, Mike. I'll now hand it back for the financials.

Mike Johnson: Thank you, Sarah. Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Mike. As Mike mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $4.5 billion, up 20% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.1 billion, and net income was $850 million. We generated $900 million in free cash flow and returned $450 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $4.2 billion in debt and $1.8 billion in cash.

Good morning, everyone. I'll now turn to our realized pricing performance, which underscores the effectiveness of our disciplined hedging strategy in a volatile macro environment. As you know, realized prices represent our actual netback after production costs, transportation differentials, and the protective overlay from our derivatives book. Let me break this down by commodity, with a deep dive into the hedging mechanics.

Starting with crude oil: Our Q3 realized price averaged $76.45 per barrel, a solid 4% sequential improvement from Q2's $73.20/bbl, despite WTI spot averaging $81.50/bbl during the quarter. This reflects a few key dynamics. First, our Permian Basin heavy sour crude—primarily from our Delaware sub-basin assets—faced a $4.20/bbl discount to WTI due to persistent midstream constraints around the Waha Hub, where negative pricing flared up again in late September amid takeaway capacity lags from Enterprise's Matterhorn expansion delays. Regionally, our Eagle Ford light sweet production realized a tighter $1.80/bbl discount to WTI, benefiting from improved connectivity to Corpus Christi export terminals.

Now, turning to natural gas: We realized $2.65 per MCF, up 12% from Q2's $2.37/MCF, even as Henry Hub spot dipped to an average of $2.90/MMBtu. This was driven by our Haynesville Shale portfolio, where rich-gas economics yielded a $0.25/MCF premium after NGL recoveries—think C3+ liquids tipping out at around 120 barrels per MMcf equivalent. However, Appalachia exposure dragged with a $0.40/MCF basis penalty to Dominion South, exacerbated by storage injections peaking at 3.2 Bcf/d and muted LNG feedgas demand ahead of Freeport LNG's Train 3 restart.

These realized prices would have been far more volatile without our hedging programs—our true differentiator in risk-adjusted returns. We maintain a pragmatic, multi-basin hedging overlay covering 55-65% of forecasted production across a 24-month forward curve, layered opportunistically to capture upside while flooring downside. Let me walk you through the Q3 impact and our book.

For oil, hedges contributed a +$2.10/bbl uplift to realized pricing, turning what could have been a $5-7/bbl spot-to-realized gap into a manageable premium. Specifically:

55% of Q3 volumes were under fixed-price swaps averaging $75.00/bbl for the quarter (NYMEX WTI basis).

20% in collars with floors at $70/bbl and caps at $85/bbl—exercising nicely as WTI traded in that band 80% of the time.

No puts outstanding, preserving premium for debt paydown.

This buffered the 15% intra-quarter WTI volatility spike from Red Sea disruptions and OPEC+ extension signals. Looking forward, we've added 40% coverage for Q4 2024 at $78.50/bbl swaps, and 25% for 2025 at $75/bbl, rolled from our Q4 '23 book when forwards were sub-$70.

On gas, hedging added +$0.35/MCF, critical amid Henry Hub's 25% standard deviation. Breakdown:

60% swapped at $2.75/MMBtu (fixed to Henry Hub).

15% three-way collars: $2.50 floor / $3.50 ceiling / $4.00 cap—zero-cost structures we layered in June at the NYMEX strip low.

Basis swaps hedged 30% of Haynesville volumes at +$0.10 to Henry Hub, mitigating Waha-like blowouts.

Without this, our gas realizations could have dipped below $2.00/MCF during the shoulder season softness. Strategically, we're tilting toward more collars post-Q3 to balance protection—about 70% hedged now vs. 90% swaps last year—allowing participation in potential AI data center demand ramps, with U.S. LNG exports projected at 14 Bcf/d by year-end per EIA outlooks.

To quantify the full-year impact: Hedging is on track to deliver $150-175 million in risk-adjusted value, equivalent to 8-10% of our upstream EBITDAX guidance. Our counterparties—JPMorgan, Goldman Sachs, and BP—remain investment-grade, with a net undrawn RBL facility providing dry powder for opportunistic layering.

In summary, our realized prices reflect resilient operations in the Permian and Haynesville, tempered by basin-specific basis but fortified by hedging discipline. This positions us to generate 15-20% ROCE through the cycle, even if WTI moderates to $75/bbl and gas holds $2.75.

Before I move on, I'd like to spend a few minutes on one of our core value drivers: our proved reserves additions, reserve replacement ratio, or RRR, and the strength of our organic growth program. As you know, in our industry, sustaining and growing the reserve base is the bedrock of long-term free cash flow generation and shareholder returns, especially in a macro environment where WTI has held above $75 per barrel and Brent around $80, buoyed by ongoing OPEC+ cuts and resilient global demand.

Let me start with the headline numbers, which we released in our 10-Q this morning. For the first nine months of 2024, we added 452 million barrels of oil equivalent, or MMboe, to our proved reserves base. This brings our Q3-end total proved reserves to 2.8 billion boe, up 18% from year-end 2023. To put this in context, our 2024 production year-to-date averaged 248 MMboe, reflecting a 12% year-over-year increase driven by our high-margin assets. This translates to a three-year average RRR of 182%—well above the industry benchmark of 100%—and a trailing nine-month RRR of 182%, marking our ninth straight year above 150%. For comparison, peers like Pioneer Natural Resources reported around 140% and EOG Resources closer to 160% on a three-year basis; we're proud to lead the pack here.

Crucially, 93% of these additions—420 MMboe—were organic, coming from extensions, discoveries, and positive revisions through our own exploration and development efforts. The remaining 32 MMboe stemmed from minor bolt-on acquisitions in the DJ Basin, which were opportunistic and accretive at under $5/boe. This organic focus underscores our strategy of high-grading our portfolio toward Tier 1 acreage with deep inventory, avoiding the dilution risks of large-scale M&A we've seen some competitors chase.

Breaking it down by reserve category, using the SEC definitions: proved developed producing, or PDP, additions totaled 185 MMboe, primarily from successful infill drilling and improved well performance. Proved developed non-producing, or PDNP, added 92 MMboe, tied to facility tie-ins and behind-pipe opportunities. The lion's share, however, was in proved undeveloped, or PUD, locations—175 MMboe—reflecting our aggressive delineation of 5-year development plans. Positive technical revisions contributed another 45 MMboe, driven by outperformance in estimated ultimate recovery, or EURs, where our average Permian well is now booking 1.2 MMboe EURs, up 15% from prior type curves.

Now, let's zoom in regionally, as performance varied but all basins delivered. Our Permian Basin assets in the Delaware and Midland sub-basins accounted for 62% of additions, or 280 MMboe. Here, organic growth was turbocharged by technical innovations: we deployed extended-reach laterals averaging 12,500 feet, up from 10,000 feet in 2023, combined with our 'ApexMax' completion design—featuring 60 pounds of proppant per foot and dissolvable diverters—which boosted initial production rates by 25% to over 1,800 boe/d per well. This led to 140 MMboe in PUD bookings from 450 net locations, giving us a 10-year drilling inventory of 3,200 locations at sub-$40/boe breakevens. Compared to Occidental or ConocoPhillips' Midland results, our Delaware Wolfcamp C interval is proving richer in liquids, with 65% oil cut.

In the Eagle Ford Shale, which makes up 22% of our portfolio, we added 95 MMboe, all organic. Our Pearsall and Lower Eagle Ford benches responded well to refrac pilots—five operations in Q2/Q3 yielded 30% EUR uplift—and appraisal drilling confirmed a new 20-section development block with 200 PUD locations. This region's shallow decline profile and proximity to Gulf Coast markets continue to deliver mid-teens IRRs even at $60 WTI.

Bakken/Three Forks in the Williston Basin contributed 68 MMboe, or 15% of total additions, highlighted by a major extension play in our Parshall Field position, where high-density frac pilots increased parent-child interference mitigation by 40%. We're now converting 120 gross locations to PUDs, with breakevens dipping below $45/boe amid improving service costs.

Internationally, our offshore Gulf of Mexico assets added 9 MMboe, including positive revisions from the Anchor development, where subsea tiebacks to our existing Lucius platform unlocked incremental proved volumes ahead of first oil in 2025. We're also progressing FEED engineering on a Guyana light oil discovery analog, though that's exploratory for now.

Strategically, these results reflect three pillars of our organic growth engine. First, technology-led efficiencies: We've invested $150 million in proprietary seismic reprocessing using machine learning algorithms, identifying 15% more drilling locations across our 1.2 million net acres. Our 'ReservoirSync' digital twin models are now standard, reducing dry hole risk to under 3%—half the industry average.

Second, capital discipline: All 2024 additions were economic at a $50/bbl flat price deck, aligning with our 'fortress balance sheet' ethos. This positions us to return 60% of free cash flow to shareholders via buybacks and our progressive dividend, now yielding 2.8% with 15% growth.

Third, inventory sustainability: Our developed-to-proved F&D cost was $8.20/boe, down 12% YoY, with a recycle ratio of 3.2x based on our $26/boe LOE and $45 realized price. Looking forward, we see 500+ MMboe of low-risk conversions in our 5-year plan, supporting 5-7% annual production growth through 2028 without incremental acreage spend.

Of course, risks remain: commodity volatility, regulatory hurdles like the BLM's methane rules, and the energy transition push. But with LNG export demand surging—U.S. volumes up 10% YoY—and oil fundamentals intact per EIA forecasts, our low-cost, oil-weighted portfolio (72% oil/liquids) is primed for outsized returns.

In summary, our 182% RRR and 93% organic additions not only replace but grow reserves at compelling economics, fueling our path to $5 billion in cumulative FCF by 2027.

Turning now to our refining segment, which continues to be a cornerstone of Apex Energy's integrated model, delivering robust profitability amid a volatile macro environment. In Q3, we processed a record 452,000 barrels per day on average across our three high-complexity refineries—the 250,000 bpd Gulf Coast facility in Texas, the 150,000 bpd Midwest hub in Illinois, and our 100,000 bpd West Coast plant in California. This represents a 5.7% increase quarter-over-quarter from 427,000 bpd in Q2 and a solid 3.2% year-over-year gain, driven by strong operational uptime and favorable regional crude slates.

Capacity utilization hit an impressive 95.2%, up from 90% in Q2, as we successfully ramped post-turnaround activities at the Gulf Coast site. For context, this outperforms the USGC peer average of 92%, per EIA data, and reflects our disciplined maintenance strategy—we completed a 35-day partial turnaround on the Gulf Coast hydrocracker ahead of schedule, minimizing offline days to just 12% of the quarter versus our guided 15-18%. Throughput was bolstered by optimized crude sourcing: 60% WTI and Eagle Ford light slates from our upstream assets, blended with 25% imported Canadian heavy via the Keystone Pipeline, and 15% Brent-par imports to maximize Nelson Complexity Index yields. Our effective NCI of 11.2 across the portfolio continues to give us a competitive edge over simpler peers like Valero's lower-complexity plants.

On margins, we realized a strong $15.80 per barrel in Q3, a 22% QoQ uplift from $12.95, though down 8% YoY from the exceptional $17.20 amid peak post-COVID demand. This was paced by the benchmark 3-2-1 crack spread averaging $18.40 on the USGC—up 25% QoQ on summer driving season diesel demand and jet fuel recovery—while Singapore GRMs held steady at $14.50, supporting our export book. Regionally, Gulf Coast margins shone at $17.20/bbl, fueled by 2-1 diesel cracks hitting $28 amid trucking and export surges to Europe, where Russian sanctions have tightened supply. Midwest margins were solid at $14.50, benefiting from PADD 2 distillate premiums, though tempered by competitive rail-unload economics versus BP and Marathon's Toledo plants. West Coast lagged at $13.80 due to elevated CARB-compliant fuel costs and refinery rationalizations by Phillips 66, but our preemptive renewable diesel blending—now at 5% of output—mitigated this, capturing $2.50/bbl premiums.

Gross refining margins benefited from a favorable 65/35 diesel/gasoline yield mix, with distillate yields up 2 points QoQ to 48% thanks to hydrocracker optimization. Feedstock costs averaged $68/bbl WTI equivalent, 10% below NYMEX settles, underscoring our upstream integration advantage—internal crudes accounted for 55% of runs, saving $1.20/bbl versus third-party purchases. We hedged 40% of Q3 cracks at $16.50 floor via swaps, protecting against the mid-quarter Brent spike to $85.

Operationally, we're firing on all cylinders with efficiency metrics at multi-year lows. Cash operating expenses per barrel fell 12% QoQ to $4.10 from $4.65, beating our guidance and the peer median of $4.80 per OPIS. This was driven by three key initiatives: First, our digital twin platform, powered by AspenTech's AI-driven optimizer, improved crude assay precision by 15%, boosting clean product yields 1.8 points to 87.5% and cutting off-spec production by 20%. Second, energy efficiency gains shaved 8% off utility costs—our Gulf Coast FCCU now runs at 112% design severity with 5% lower natural gas consumption via steam recovery upgrades. Third, the rollout of our proprietary 'YieldMax' process—enhancing alkylation units with ionic liquid catalysts, akin to Chevron's advancements—lifted gasoline octane by 2 RON points, enabling 10% higher value product pricing.

Regionally, Gulf Coast ops remain our profit engine, with export volumes up 18% YoY to 120,000 bpd, capturing LatAm arbitrage windows. Midwest throughput grew 7% on renewable diesel co-processing, positioning us for IRA tax credits worth $0.50/bbl next year. West Coast efficiency offset regulatory headwinds, with SOx emissions down 25% post-scrubber installs.

Strategically, we're advancing Project Phoenix: a $450 million investment to add 20,000 bpd renewable diesel capacity at Gulf Coast by Q4 2025, targeting 15-20% segment EBITDA growth through 2026. Turnarounds are front-loaded—next major at Midwest Q1 2025—keeping 2024 utilization at 93-95%. With cracks firming on winter distillate draws and OPEC+ cuts supporting $75+ crude, we see Q4 margins at $16-18/bbl, with full-year refining EBITDA up 15% to $1.2 billion.

Overall, refining underscores Apex's resilience—high-complexity assets, integrated supply chains, and tech-led efficiencies de-risking us in downturns while capturing upside.

I will now turn the call over to Tom Rivera for an operational update.

Tom Rivera: Thank you, Lisa. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 450,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. We successfully brought Blackhawk Federal 12H-34 online, which is expected to contribute significantly to our production growth in the coming quarters. We are also making progress on our cost reduction initiatives, with drilling costs down 8% year-over-year through optimized practices.

Now I will turn it over to David Lee for an update on our exploration activities.

David Lee: Thank you, Tom. We are excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Delaware Basin and are planning to drill 140 exploration wells in the next year. We believe these wells have the potential to add significant reserves to our portfolio.

Good morning, everyone. I'd now like to turn to our exploration and drilling activity updates, where we've continued to execute with discipline amid a supportive macro environment—WTI holding steady around $76 per barrel and Henry Hub natural gas at $2.85 per mmbtu. Our team has delivered strong operational momentum, with key well results exceeding our internal type curves and positioning us for multi-year inventory sustainability. Let me break this down by highlighting recent results, regional performance, technical advancements, and our forward DDP.

Starting with the numbers: In Q3, we spudded 28 wells across our core acreage, brought online 32 gross wells—24.6 net—and maintained an active rig count of 7, split between 5 in the Permian and 2 in the Eagle Ford. This represents a 15% sequential increase in completions from Q2, driven by improved pad drilling efficiencies. Total D&C capex came in at $285 million, or about 28% of our full-year guidance midpoint, with drilling costs averaging $820 per lateral foot in the Permian—down 8% year-over-year due to optimized slide drilling and PDC bit performance from our vendor partners like Halliburton and Schlumberger.

Key Well Results

Let's dive into the highlights. In the Delaware Basin—our premier asset comprising 65% of our D&C activity—the standout was the Blackhawk Federal 12H-34 well in Lea County, New Mexico. This 2-mile lateral in the Wolfcamp A targeted a cleaner, oilier bench and posted an IP30 rate of 1,450 boe/d (82% oil), smashing our 1,200 boe/d type curve by 21%. With 45 stages, 2,200 lbs/ft proppant intensity, and 15-foot cluster spacing, we're seeing EURs north of 1.4 million boe based on our decline curve analytics—powered by our proprietary ResFrac modeling. This well's 30-day peak outperformed peers like Pioneer and Occidental by 10-15% on a normalized basis, with a sub-$40 WTI half-cycle breakeven.

Complementing this, our four-well pad in the Antelope Ridge prospect delivered an average IP30 of 1,180 boe/d, with 24-hour peaks exceeding 2,200 boe/d. These results underscore the repeatability of our Second Bone Spring play, where we've now delineated 180 gross locations with IRRs above 60% at current strips.

Shifting east to the Eagle Ford, our Pearsall Shale pilot—two wells in Dimmit County—yielded promising gas/oil mix results: IP30s of 850 boe/d (45% liquids) on 10,000-foot laterals. While early in the learning curve, these beat our pre-drill estimates by 12%, with completion costs at $650 per foot thanks to diverter tech reducing screen-outs. We're encouraged by the condensate yields, which hedge our gas exposure amid volatile NGL prices.

Internationally, our 30% JV stake in the Suriname Block 58 offshore campaign—partnered with TotalEnergies—saw the first appraisal well, Krabdagu-1, flow 5,200 bbls/d of 34-degree API oil on DST, confirming a 400-million-barrel column extension. This de-risks 10+ follow-on locations under our PSA terms.

Trends and Technical Initiatives

Performance trends are robust: Q3 Permian fleetwide IP30 averaged 1,220 boe/d, up 18% from Q2 and 25% above basin benchmarks per Enverus analytics. Cycle times compressed to 42 days from spud to sales—best-in-class—via simultaneous ops and our AI-driven geosteering platform from Baker Hughes, which cut doglegs by 20%. On the completion side, we're pushing the envelope with 'super-zipper' fracs on multi-well pads, incorporating 100-mesh sand for far-field fracture complexity and dissolvable balls for faster flowback. This has boosted our 60-day recoveries by 15% while holding tail-end declines to 65% annually.

We've also launched a carbon-neutral drilling pilot in the Permian using electrified rigs from Nabors, targeting Scope 1 emissions reductions of 40%—aligning with our net-zero 2050 pledge and appealing to ESG-focused investors.

Regional Commentary

Permian (85% of 2024 D&C capex): Inventory stands at 1,200 gross locations (950 net), with 70% Tier 1. We're layering in Wolfcamp C opportunities via a recent 5,000-acre farm-in from ConocoPhillips, adding 50 locations at $150/acre.

Eagle Ford: Steady-state with 10 rigs planned for 2025; focus on liquids-rich Pearsall to counter Haynesville gas oversupply.

Emerging: Scouting DJ Basin Niobrara extensions and a GoM shelf lease round entry, leveraging our seismic library.

Future Plans and Strategic Insights

Looking ahead, our 2025 DDP ramps to 140 gross wells (105 net), with $1.2-1.3 billion capex—40% front-loaded. We'll add two Permian rigs in Q1, targeting 35 completions per rig per year. AFE approvals total $450 million for H1, including a 10-well Wolfcamp demo and Suriname sidetrack.

Strategically, we're prioritizing capital velocity: 90% D&C allocation to assets with sub-$45 breakevens and >50% IRRs, hedging 60% of 2025 oil at $73.50. In a $70-85 WTI world, this yields 2.5x FCF returns. We're also pursuing bolt-on M&A—$200-300 million dry powder—for Permian stack pay, echoing EQT's recent moves. Risks remain around service inflation (up 5% QoQ) and regulatory hurdles like New Mexico setbacks, but our 3.5-year drilled inventory provides optionality.

In summary, these results validate our tech-driven, basin-centric strategy, delivering shareholder value through superior returns.

Finally, I'll turn it over to Emily Carter to discuss our marketing strategy.

Emily Carter: Thank you, David. We are focused on optimizing our marketing strategy to maximize the value of our production. We are seeing strong demand for renewable diesel in the Gulf Coast market area, and we are working to expand our customer base and strengthen our relationships with existing customers. The impact of this product is significant, with exports up 18% year-over-year and premiums capturing additional value through our integrated downstream operations.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. We will pause momentarily to assemble our roster. Our first question comes from Chris Thompson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Chris Thompson: Good morning. Can you provide more detail on your hedging program and its impact on realized prices?

Mike Johnson: Good morning, Chris. As Lisa detailed earlier, our hedging has been a key stabilizer, providing a $2.10/bbl uplift on oil and $0.35/MCF on gas this quarter, with 55-65% coverage layered prudently. We're positioned well for volatility ahead.

Operator: Our next question comes from Anna Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Anna Patel: Good morning. What are your expectations for future capex and development plans?

Lisa Chen: Good morning, Anna. Great question, and thanks for joining the call. I'll dive into this in detail, as our future development plans and resource potential form the bedrock of Apex's long-term value creation. We're laser-focused on high-return inventory, capital efficiency, and integrating ESG imperatives into our strategy. Let me break it down by key regions, with specifics on our drilling inventory, resource upside, and technical initiatives.

First, a high-level overview. As of Q3-end 2024, our proved developed producing reserves—or PDP—stand at 1.2 billion barrels of oil equivalent, or BOE, with total proved reserves at 2.8 BBOE. That's up 12% year-over-year, driven by strong well performance and acquisitions. But the real story is our 2P reserves—proved plus probable—which clock in at 5.1 BBOE, and our total resource potential, including contingent and prospective resources, exceeds 15 BBOE on a risked basis. This gives us over a decade of drilling inventory at current paces, with an average NPV10 of $25 per BOE across the portfolio, assuming a $70 WTI flat deck.

Our five-year plan calls for $12-15 billion in capex, ramping to $3.5 billion in 2025, focused on 650-700 gross operated wells. We're targeting 8-10% annual production growth through 2028, taking total output from 450,000 BOE per day today to over 650,000 BOE/d, with oil comprising 65% of the mix. Returns remain robust: full-cycle DD&A costs are sub-$25/BOE, and we're generating 40-50% IRRs on new drills at current strips.

Let's drill down regionally, starting with our crown jewel: the Permian Basin, where we hold 450,000 net acres across the Delaware and Midland basins. This is our growth engine, representing 70% of our inventory. We've got 4,500+ locations queued up, with half in the high-pressure, high-temp Wolfcamp A and Bone Springs intervals. Recent pads—like our Buckeye 10-well pilot—are crushing it: 2,500 lateral feet per stage, 4,000-5,000 BOE initial production per well, and 60-day rates averaging 1,800 bbl/d oil. We're pushing the envelope with our "Permian Plus" initiative: integrating AI-driven seismic inversion and fiber-optic DAS monitoring to optimize frac designs. This has boosted EURs by 15-20% on recent vintages, from 1.2 MMBOE to 1.4+ MMBOE per well.

Capex here is $2.2 billion in '25, funding 450 wells. Resource upside? Our unrisked 2C contingent resources add another 3 BBOE, with a key focus on the Second Bone Springs—think ExxonMobil's recent Pioneer deal analogs, where we've identified 800 halo locations via machine learning reservoir models. Stacked pays give us multi-zone development efficiency, dropping breakevens to $35-40 WTI.

Shifting to the Gulf of Mexico, our deepwater portfolio shines for its low decline and high margins. We operate three major assets: the Olympus field (25% WI), Trident (40% WI), and our flagship Dorado discovery. Proved reserves here are 450 MMBOE, but total resource potential is 1.5 BBOE unrisked, including 1 Tcf of associated gas.

Development kicks off Q3 '25 with the $1.2 billion Dorado FPSO tie-back—subsalt Lower Tertiary, flowing at 50,000 bbl/d gross peak. We're partnering with Shell on subsea boosting tech to accelerate ramp-up, targeting first oil by mid-'26. LOE is just $8/BOE, with 25+ year reservoir lives. Amid OPEC+ cuts and rising Asian LNG demand, we're advancing Dorado's gas to a potential 200 MMcf/d hub, monetizing via Gulf Coast pipelines or even FLNG floats like those from New Fortress Energy.

Technical edge: We've deployed permanent electromagnetic reservoir monitoring—EMRM—to track fluid fronts in real-time, de-risking EOR pilots. Early results show 10-15% recovery uplift via low-sal polymer floods, pushing recovery factors from 25% to 35%+.

Internationally, Guyana's our wildcard for outsized returns. Through our 20% non-op stake in Block Z—analogous to ExxonMobil's Stabroek— we've certified 800 MMBOE net 2P reserves from Liza Phase 3 and Payara. Resource potential jumps to 2 BBOE unrisked across five prospects, with Yellowtail sanction imminent. Hess-style pay zones here are 100m+ thick, with 25-30% porosities. Our plan: Drill 10 appraisal wells over two years, with FID targeted for '27. At $60 Brent, this delivers 60%+ IRRs.

In the North Sea, we're steady-state: 150 MMBOE 1P in the Buzzard field (JV with Suncor and Siccar Point), with CCS potential via the Acorn hub. We're injecting 1 MMtpa CO2 this year via our Northern Lights partnership, qualifying for UK CCUS subsidies and extending field life by 10 years.

Strategically, we're optimizing via M&A and tech. We closed the $2.5 billion Eagle Ford bolt-on last quarter, adding 300 low-breakeven locations. Trends favor us: WTI-Brent spreads narrowing to $4, RBNZ efficiencies hitting 1,200 ft/day ROPs, and LNG demand growing 4% CAGR per Shell's LTGMR. But we're not ignoring transition: 20% of capex goes to CCUS, electrification (e.g., Chevron-style e-frac fleets), and hydrogen pilots in the Permian.

Risks? Volatility from Iran tensions or EV adoption, but our hedge book covers 60% of '25 oil at $75. Sensitivities: $10 WTI move swings FCF by $1.2 billion. Overall, this portfolio positions Apex for 15-20% ROCE through the cycle.

Anna, does that cover it, or want more color on Guyana certs?

Operator: Our next question comes from Robert Kline with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Robert Kline: Could you please provide more color on your production costs and operational efficiencies?

Tom Rivera: Good morning, Robert. Absolutely. We've driven costs down through efficiencies like extended laterals and optimized completions, with LOE at $26/boe and drilling costs at $820 per lateral foot. Our cycle times are best-in-class at 42 days, supporting strong returns.

Operator: Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Citi. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

David Lee: Thanks, Laura. The strong results from wells like Blackhawk Federal directly bolster our inventory, adding over 180 locations in Second Bone Spring alone. This shifts our strategy toward accelerated Permian development, with 140 wells planned in 2025, maintaining sub-$45 breakevens and enhancing long-term growth optionality.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mark Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mark Rivera: What is the outlook for the new product in the coming years?

Emily Carter: Good morning, Mark. Renewable diesel outlook is bright, with Project Phoenix adding 20,000 bpd capacity by Q4 2025. We're targeting 15-20% EBITDA growth in refining through 2026, leveraging IRA credits and strong Gulf Coast demand, with margins holding firm at $16-18/bbl in Q4.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Mike Johnson for closing remarks.

Mike Johnson: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.
